1: //! The fixed-size 16-byte Pathland opcode.
2: //!
3: //! Layout (see `spec/OPCODE.md`):
4: //!
5: //! ```text
6: //! [Category: u8][Command: u8][Flags: u16][A: u32][B: u32][C: u32]
7: //! ```
8: //!
9: //! All multi-byte fields are little-endian on the wire. `size_of::<Opcode>() == 16`,
10: //! so a 64-byte cache line holds exactly 4 opcodes.
11: 
12: use core::ptr;
13: 
14: /// Size of one opcode in bytes.
15: pub const OPCODE_SIZE: usize = 16;
16: 
17: /// A fixed-size 16-byte opcode.
18: ///
19: /// This struct intentionally mirrors the wire layout and is `#[repr(C, packed)]`
20: /// per the specification. Because it is packed, fields may be unaligned; always
21: /// read fields through the accessor methods (which use unaligned reads) rather
22: /// than by value.
23: #[repr(C, packed)]
24: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
25: pub struct Opcode {
26:     /// Opcode category (see `constants::Category`).
27:     pub category: u8,
28:     /// Command within the category (see `constants::Command*`).
29:     pub command: u8,
30:     /// Category/command-specific flags.
31:     pub flags: u16,
32:     /// Primary payload.
33:     pub a: u32,
34:     /// Secondary payload.
35:     pub b: u32,
36:     /// Tertiary payload.
37:     pub c: u32,
38: }
39: 
40: impl Opcode {
41:     /// Byte size of an opcode (`16`).
42:     pub const SIZE: usize = OPCODE_SIZE;
43: 
44:     /// Construct an opcode from raw fields.
45:     #[inline]
46:     pub const fn new(category: u8, command: u8, flags: u16, a: u32, b: u32, c: u32) -> Self {
47:         Self {
48:             category,
49:             command,
50:             flags,
51:             a,
52:             b,
53:             c,
54:         }
55:     }
56: 
57:     /// The opcode category.
58:     #[inline]
59:     pub fn category(&self) -> u8 {
60:         self.category
61:     }
62: 
63:     /// The command within the category.
64:     #[inline]
65:     pub fn command(&self) -> u8 {
66:         self.command
67:     }
68: 
69:     /// The 16-bit flags word.
70:     #[inline]
71:     pub fn flags(&self) -> u16 {
72:         // SAFETY: read_unaligned is well-defined for packed fields.
73:         unsafe { ptr::addr_of!(self.flags).read_unaligned() }
74:     }
75: 
76:     /// Primary payload (little-endian u32).
77:     #[inline]
78:     pub fn a(&self) -> u32 {
79:         // SAFETY: read_unaligned is well-defined for packed fields.
80:         unsafe { ptr::addr_of!(self.a).read_unaligned() }
81:     }
82: 
83:     /// Secondary payload (little-endian u32).
84:     #[inline]
85:     pub fn b(&self) -> u32 {
86:         // SAFETY: read_unaligned is well-defined for packed fields.
87:         unsafe { ptr::addr_of!(self.b).read_unaligned() }
88:     }
89: 
90:     /// Tertiary payload (little-endian u32).
91:     #[inline]
92:     pub fn c(&self) -> u32 {
93:         // SAFETY: read_unaligned is well-defined for packed fields.
94:         unsafe { ptr::addr_of!(self.c).read_unaligned() }
95:     }
96: 
97:     /// Interpret `A` as an `f32` (bit-preserving).
98:     #[inline]
99:     pub fn a_f32(&self) -> f32 {
100:         f32::from_bits(self.a())
101:     }
102: 
103:     /// Interpret `B` as an `f32` (bit-preserving).
104:     #[inline]
105:     pub fn b_f32(&self) -> f32 {
106:         f32::from_bits(self.b())
107:     }
108: 
109:     /// Interpret `C` as an `f32` (bit-preserving).
110:     #[inline]
111:     pub fn c_f32(&self) -> f32 {
112:         f32::from_bits(self.c())
113:     }
114: 
115:     /// Serialize to the 16-byte wire representation (little-endian).
116:     pub fn to_bytes(&self) -> [u8; OPCODE_SIZE] {
117:         let mut out = [0u8; OPCODE_SIZE];
118:         out[0] = self.category;
119:         out[1] = self.command;
120:         // SAFETY: read_unaligned is well-defined for packed fields.
121:         let flags = unsafe { ptr::addr_of!(self.flags).read_unaligned() };
122:         let a = unsafe { ptr::addr_of!(self.a).read_unaligned() };
123:         let b = unsafe { ptr::addr_of!(self.b).read_unaligned() };
124:         let c = unsafe { ptr::addr_of!(self.c).read_unaligned() };
125:         out[2..4].copy_from_slice(&flags.to_le_bytes());
126:         out[4..8].copy_from_slice(&a.to_le_bytes());
127:         out[8..12].copy_from_slice(&b.to_le_bytes());
128:         out[12..16].copy_from_slice(&c.to_le_bytes());
129:         out
130:     }
131: 
132:     /// Deserialize from the 16-byte wire representation (little-endian).
133:     pub fn from_bytes(bytes: &[u8; OPCODE_SIZE]) -> Self {
134:         let category = bytes[0];
135:         let command = bytes[1];
136:         let flags = u16::from_le_bytes([bytes[2], bytes[3]]);
137:         let a = u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[4..8].try_into().unwrap());
138:         let b = u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[8..12].try_into().unwrap());
139:         let c = u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[12..16].try_into().unwrap());
140:         Self {
141:             category,
142:             command,
143:             flags,
144:             a,
145:             b,
146:             c,
147:         }
148:     }
149: }
150: 
151: #[cfg(test)]
152: mod tests {
153:     use super::*;
154: 
155:     #[test]
156:     fn size_is_16_bytes() {
157:         assert_eq!(core::mem::size_of::<Opcode>(), 16);
158:     }
159: 
160:     #[test]
161:     fn round_trips_through_bytes() {
162:         let op = Opcode::new(0x01, 0x01, 0x0001, 0x1122_3344, 0x5566_7788, 0x99AA_BBCC);
163:         let bytes = op.to_bytes();
164:         let back = Opcode::from_bytes(&bytes);
165:         assert_eq!(op, back);
166:     }
167: 
168:     #[test]
169:     fn known_byte_layout() {
170:         // TREE / CREATE_NODE, no flags, nodeId=1, componentType=VSTACK(0x0010), c=0
171:         let op = Opcode::new(0x01, 0x01, 0x0000, 1, 0x0010, 0);
172:         assert_eq!(
173:             op.to_bytes(),
174:             [0x01, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x10, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00]
175:         );
176:     }
177: 
178:     #[test]
179:     fn float_payloads_round_trip() {
180:         let op = Opcode::new(0x02, 0x01, 0, 42, 100.0f32.to_bits(), 200.0f32.to_bits());
181:         let back = Opcode::from_bytes(&op.to_bytes());
182:         assert_eq!(back.a(), 42);
183:         assert_eq!(back.b_f32(), 100.0);
184:         assert_eq!(back.c_f32(), 200.0);
185:     }
186: }

(End of file - total 186 lines)
</content>

1: //! Protocol constants: categories, commands, component types, value types, flags.
2: //!
3: //! These constants are part of the wire protocol (see `spec/OPCODE.md`) and MUST
4: //! NOT be renumbered once released. Component types were renumbered pre-release
5: //! to the grouped ranges in `spec/PRIMITIVES.md` (wire version stays 1).
6: 
7: /// Opcode categories (`Category` field, u8).
8: pub mod category {
9:     /// Tree mutations (guest → host): node create/delete/insert/remove/move.
10:     pub const TREE: u8 = 0x01;
11:     /// Parameters and design tokens (guest → host): the constraint properties
12:     /// (spacing, padding, alignment, …) and content that native renderers use
13:     /// to lay out and style native elements. The engine does NOT emit rects.
14:     pub const PARAMETER: u8 = 0x02;
15:     /// Raw input events (host → guest): pointer down/move/up, key down/up.
16:     pub const EVENT: u8 = 0x03;
17:     /// Control (both directions): reset, environment, custom data.
18:     pub const META: u8 = 0x04;
19: }
20: 
21: /// Commands within the `TREE` category.
22: pub mod tree {
23:     /// `A=nodeId, B=componentType (u16, low)`
24:     pub const CREATE_NODE: u8 = 0x01;
25:     /// `A=nodeId`
26:     pub const DELETE_NODE: u8 = 0x02;
27:     /// `A=parentId, B=childId, C=index` (append is `C = u32::MAX`, see [`crate::APPEND`])
28:     pub const INSERT_CHILD: u8 = 0x03;
29:     /// `A=parentId, B=childId`
30:     pub const REMOVE_CHILD: u8 = 0x04;
31:     /// `A=parentId, B=childId, C=newIndex` (append is `C = u32::MAX`, see [`crate::APPEND`])
32:     pub const MOVE_CHILD: u8 = 0x05;
33: }
34: 
35: /// Commands within the `PARAMETER` category.
36: pub mod parameter {
37:     /// `A=nodeId, B=(valueType << 16) | propertyId, C=value`
38:     pub const SET_PROPERTY: u8 = 0x01;
39:     /// `A=arenaRef (path), B=valueType (u8), C=value`
40:     pub const SET_DESIGN_TOKEN: u8 = 0x02;
41:     /// `A=nodeId, B=arenaRef (utf8)`
42:     pub const SET_TEXT: u8 = 0x03;
43:     /// **Draft.** `A=nodeId, B=days since epoch (I32), C=millis of day (U32)` —
44:     /// set a node's date value (e.g. a `DATE_PICKER`); see
45:     /// `spec/PRIMITIVES.md` / `spec/OPCODE.md`.
46:     pub const SET_DATE: u8 = 0x04;
47: }
48: 
49: /// Commands within the `EVENT` category.
50: ///
51: /// Events are **raw inputs** (host → guest), each carrying a host-resolved
52: /// `targetId`. High-level interpretations (tap, drag, long-press) are built by
53: /// the guest/app from these raw inputs and are NOT part of the protocol.
54: pub mod event {
55:     /// `A=targetId, B=x (f32), C=y (f32)` (Flags `POINTER_SECONDARY`)
56:     pub const POINTER_DOWN: u8 = 0x01;
57:     /// `A=targetId, B=x (f32), C=y (f32)` (Flags `HOVER_ENTER` / `HOVER_LEAVE`)
58:     pub const POINTER_MOVE: u8 = 0x02;
59:     /// `A=targetId, B=x (f32), C=y (f32)` (Flags `POINTER_SECONDARY`)
60:     pub const POINTER_UP: u8 = 0x03;
61:     /// `A=targetId, B=keyCode (u16, low), C=modifiers (u8, low)` (Flags `KEY_REPEAT`)
62:     pub const KEY_DOWN: u8 = 0x04;
63:     /// `A=targetId, B=keyCode (u16, low), C=modifiers (u8, low)`
64:     pub const KEY_UP: u8 = 0x05;
65:     /// `A=targetId, B=value (f32)` — a control's value changed (host → guest).
66:     /// The renderer resolves the control's semantic value (e.g. a slider thumb
67:     /// dragged to a point on its track); the guest/app writes it into its state.
68:     pub const VALUE_CHANGED: u8 = 0x06;
69:     /// `A=targetId, B=string offset` — a text field's value changed (host →
70:     /// guest). The new text lives in the batch's string section, referenced by
71:     /// the *relative* offset in `B` (the same convention as `PARAMETER::SET_TEXT`).
72:     pub const TEXT_CHANGED: u8 = 0x07;
73:     /// **Draft.** `A=targetId, B=focused (0/1)` — a node gained/lost focus.
74:     pub const FOCUS_CHANGED: u8 = 0x08;
75:     /// **Draft.** `A=targetId, B=editing (0/1)` — an editing session began/ended.
76:     pub const EDITING_CHANGED: u8 = 0x09;
77:     /// **Draft.** `A=targetId, B=0` — the user committed a field (onSubmit).
78:     pub const SUBMIT: u8 = 0x0A;
79:     /// **Draft.** `A=targetId, B=offsetX (f32), C=offsetY (f32)` — scroll offset.
80:     pub const SCROLL: u8 = 0x0B;
81:     /// **Draft.** `A=targetId, B=deltaX (f32), C=deltaY (f32)` — wheel/trackpad.
82:     pub const WHEEL: u8 = 0x0C;
83:     /// **Draft.** `A=targetId, B=days since epoch (I32), C=millis of day (U32)`
84:     /// — a `DATE_PICKER`'s value changed (matches `PARAMETER::SET_DATE`).
85:     pub const DATE_CHANGED: u8 = 0x0D;
86:     /// **Draft.** Global navigation request (host → guest), never node-keyed.
87:     /// With the `NAVIGATE_URL` flag, `B` is a string offset (event arena /
88:     /// batch string section) to the destination URL; without it, the event means
89:     /// "back one step" (native back affordance) and `B`/`C` are ignored.
90:     pub const NAVIGATE: u8 = 0x0E;
91:     /// **Draft.** A bound `AUDIO`/`VIDEO` node's playback state changed
92:     /// (host → guest); `B` = 0/1. Reported only when `PLAYBACK_STATE` is bound.
93:     pub const MEDIA_PLAY_STATE_CHANGED: u8 = 0x0F;
94:     /// **Draft.** A bound media node's current position (host → guest); `B` =
95:     /// seconds (f32). Reported while playing; an app-initiated seek is not echoed.
96:     pub const MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED: u8 = 0x10;
97:     /// **Draft.** A bound media node reached the end of its media (host → guest).
98:     pub const MEDIA_ENDED: u8 = 0x11;
99:     /// **Draft.** A bound media node's volume changed (host → guest); `B` =
100:     /// volume (f32, 0..1).
101:     pub const MEDIA_VOLUME_CHANGED: u8 = 0x12;
102: }
103: 
104: /// Commands within the `META` category.
105: pub mod meta {
106:     /// Host must clear all rendered output.
107:     pub const RESET: u8 = 0x01;
108:     /// `A=fieldId (u16, low), B=field value` — a platform environment field
109:     /// (host → guest); see [`crate::environment`]. An extensible field family:
110:     /// each opcode sets one field (viewport, initial route, …).
111:     pub const ENVIRONMENT: u8 = 0x02;
112:     /// The host (renderer) requests a full snapshot of the current tree
113:     /// (host → guest). `A/B/C = 0`. Used for reconnect/gap recovery.
114:     pub const RESYNC: u8 = 0x03;
115: }
116: 
117: /// Environment field ids for `META::ENVIRONMENT` (host → guest).
118: ///
119: /// Each opcode sets one platform environment field; new fields are new ids, never
120: /// new commands (spec/OPCODE.md §Environment fields).
121: pub mod environment {
122:     /// Viewport width in logical points (f32 in `B`).
123:     pub const VIEWPORT_WIDTH: u16 = 0x0001;
124:     /// Viewport height in logical points (f32 in `B`).
125:     pub const VIEWPORT_HEIGHT: u16 = 0x0002;
126:     /// The initial route/deep-link path (STRING: `B` is a string-section/event-arena
127:     /// offset — the `TEXT_CHANGED`/`NAVIGATE` dual convention).
128:     pub const ROUTE: u16 = 0x0003;
129: }
130: 
131: /// Flag bits used across categories.
132: pub mod flag {
133:     /// `POINTER_DOWN` / `POINTER_UP`: secondary button (bit 0).
134:     pub const POINTER_SECONDARY: u16 = 0x0001;
135:     /// `POINTER_MOVE`: pointer is entering/hovering (bit 0).
136:     pub const HOVER_ENTER: u16 = 0x0001;
137:     /// `POINTER_MOVE`: pointer is leaving (bit 1).
138:     pub const HOVER_LEAVE: u16 = 0x0002;
139:     /// `KEY_DOWN`: key repeat (bit 1).
140:     pub const KEY_REPEAT: u16 = 0x0002;
141:     /// `NAVIGATE`: `B` is a URL string offset (bit 0). Without this flag the
142:     /// event is a back request.
143:     pub const NAVIGATE_URL: u16 = 0x0001;
144: }
145: 
146: /// Bits for the `EVENT_LISTENERS` semantic property (a u32 bitmask).
147: ///
148: /// Each bit requests that a renderer attach native input recognition for the
149: /// matching raw-input event and report it for that node — so any element (not
150: /// just a button) can emit raw events. Bits are independent of the `EVENT`
151: /// command ids; more event kinds can be added later.
152: pub mod listener {
153:     /// `POINTER_DOWN` events (bit 0).
154:     pub const POINTER_DOWN: u32 = 1 << 0;
155:     /// `POINTER_MOVE` events (bit 1).
156:     pub const POINTER_MOVE: u32 = 1 << 1;
157:     /// `POINTER_UP` events (bit 2).
158:     pub const POINTER_UP: u32 = 1 << 2;
159:     /// `KEY_DOWN` events (bit 3).
160:     pub const KEY_DOWN: u32 = 1 << 3;
161:     /// `KEY_UP` events (bit 4).
162:     pub const KEY_UP: u32 = 1 << 4;
163:     /// **Draft.** `FOCUS_CHANGED` events (bit 5).
164:     pub const FOCUS: u32 = 1 << 5;
165:     /// **Draft.** `EDITING_CHANGED` events (bit 6).
166:     pub const EDITING: u32 = 1 << 6;
167:     /// **Draft.** `SUBMIT` events (bit 7).
168:     pub const SUBMIT: u32 = 1 << 7;
169:     /// **Draft.** `SCROLL` events (bit 8).
170:     pub const SCROLL: u32 = 1 << 8;
171:     /// **Draft.** `WHEEL` events (bit 9).
172:     pub const WHEEL: u32 = 1 << 9;
173: 
174:     /// All pointer events (down + move + up).
175:     pub const POINTER: u32 = POINTER_DOWN | POINTER_MOVE | POINTER_UP;
176: }
177: 
178: /// Bits for the `BORDER_EDGES` style property (a u32 bitmask).
179: ///
180: /// Each bit selects one edge of a node's border. `LEADING`/`TRAILING` are
181: /// direction-aware; a renderer resolves them to physical `left`/`right`
182: /// according to its layout direction (LTR by default).
183: pub mod border_edges {
184:     /// Top edge (bit 0).
185:     pub const TOP: u32 = 1 << 0;
186:     /// Leading edge (bit 1) — physical left in LTR.
187:     pub const LEADING: u32 = 1 << 1;
188:     /// Bottom edge (bit 2).
189:     pub const BOTTOM: u32 = 1 << 2;
190:     /// Trailing edge (bit 3) — physical right in LTR.
191:     pub const TRAILING: u32 = 1 << 3;
192: 
193:     /// All four edges.
194:     pub const ALL: u32 = TOP | LEADING | BOTTOM | TRAILING;
195: }

537: /// The protocol value type for a property id.
538: ///
539: /// Color-valued properties (COLOR, BACKGROUND_COLOR, BORDER_COLOR) are emitted
540: /// with the `COLOR` value type; `EVENT_LISTENERS` and `BORDER_EDGES` are raw
541: /// `U32` bitmasks; `LABEL`/`PROMPT`/`FONT_FAMILY` are `STRING`; `LINE_LIMIT`,
542: /// `ACTION_ID`, and `BINDING_ID` are `U32`; all other constraint/style
543: /// properties are `F32` (enum-valued properties like `ALIGNMENT`/`TOGGLE_STYLE`
544: /// carry their numeric code as an `F32`). See `spec/MODIFIERS.md` for the
545: /// canonical mapping.
546: pub fn value_type_for(prop: u16) -> u8 {
547:     match prop {
548:         property_id::COLOR
549:         | property_id::BACKGROUND_COLOR
550:         | property_id::BORDER_COLOR
551:         | property_id::COLOR_VALUE
552:         | property_id::COLOR_MULTIPLY
553:         | property_id::SHADOW_COLOR
554:         | property_id::TINT => value_type::COLOR,
555:         property_id::EVENT_LISTENERS | property_id::BORDER_EDGES => value_type::U32,
556:         property_id::SELECTED
557:         | property_id::IS_SECURE
558:         | property_id::IS_INDETERMINATE
559:         | property_id::VISIBLE
560:         | property_id::ENABLED
561:         | property_id::CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS
562:         | property_id::UNDERLINE
563:         | property_id::STRIKETHROUGH
564:         | property_id::COLOR_INVERT
565:         | property_id::ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING
566:         | property_id::FIXED_SIZE_HORIZONTAL
567:         | property_id::FIXED_SIZE_VERTICAL => value_type::U8,
568:         property_id::LABEL
569:         | property_id::PROMPT
570:         | property_id::FONT_FAMILY
571:         | property_id::IMAGE_SOURCE
572:         | property_id::AUDIO_SOURCE
573:         | property_id::VIDEO_SOURCE
574:         | property_id::ROUTE => value_type::STRING,
575:         property_id::LINE_LIMIT
576:         | property_id::SELECTION
577:         | property_id::ACTION_ID
578:         | property_id::BINDING_ID
579:         | property_id::NAV_DEPTH => value_type::U32,
580:         _ => value_type::F32,
581:     }
582: }

2: //!

11: pub enum ArenaError {

14:     /// The arena offset is out of bounds or points to an invalid entry.
15:     InvalidOffset,
16: }

18: /// Allocate `bytes` into the arena region, returning its byte offset.

23:     alloc_at(data, header, crate::memory::OFF_ARENA_CURSOR, bytes)

39: /// Allocate into any arena region, using the given header cursor offset.
40: #[inline]
41: pub(crate) fn alloc_at(
42:     data: &mut [u8],
43:     header: &mut [u8],
44:     cursor_off: usize,
45:     bytes: &[u8],
46: ) -> Result<u32, ArenaError> {

48:     let len = bytes.len();
49:     let needed = 4 + len;
50:     if cursor + needed > data.len() {
51:         return Err(ArenaError::OutOfSpace);
52:     }
53:     data[cursor..cursor + 4].copy_from_slice(&(len as u32).to_le_bytes());
54:     data[cursor + 4..cursor + needed].copy_from_slice(bytes);
55:     header::set_u32(header, cursor_off, (cursor + needed) as u32);
56:     Ok(cursor as u32)

86: /// Field offsets match [`memory::OFF_*`] constants and are part of the stable
87: /// wire layout (see `spec/OPCODE.md`).
88: pub struct SharedHeader<'a> {
89:     mem: &'a [u8],
90: }
91: 
92: impl<'a> SharedHeader<'a> {
93:     /// Wrap an immutable view of the shared linear memory.
94:     pub fn new(mem: &'a [u8]) -> Self {
95:         Self { mem }
96:     }
97: 
98:     fn u32(&self, off: usize) -> u32 {
99:         u32::from_le_bytes(self.mem[off..off + 4].try_into().unwrap())
100:     }
101: 
102:     /// `frameCount` — the completed-frame watermark.
103:     pub fn frame_count(&self) -> u32 {
104:         self.u32(memory::OFF_FRAME_COUNT)
105:     }
106: 
107:     /// `readCursor` — the slot the consumer has consumed up to (masked).
108:     pub fn read_cursor(&self) -> u32 {
109:         self.u32(memory::OFF_READ_CURSOR)
110:     }
111: 
112:     /// `writeCursor` — the slot the producer has written up to (masked).
113:     pub fn write_cursor(&self) -> u32 {
114:         self.u32(memory::OFF_WRITE_CURSOR)
115:     }
116: 
117:     /// `slotCount` — number of ring slots (power of two).
118:     pub fn slot_count(&self) -> u32 {
119:         self.u32(memory::OFF_SLOT_COUNT)
120:     }
121: 
122:     /// Byte offset of the ring region within the linear memory.
123:     pub fn ring_offset(&self) -> usize {
124:         self.u32(memory::OFF_RING_OFFSET) as usize
125:     }
126: 
127:     /// Byte length of the ring region.
128:     pub fn ring_bytes(&self) -> usize {
129:         self.u32(memory::OFF_RING_BYTES) as usize
130:     }
131: 
132:     /// Byte offset of the arena region within the linear memory.
133:     pub fn arena_offset(&self) -> usize {
134:         self.u32(memory::OFF_ARENA_OFFSET) as usize
135:     }
136: 
137:     /// Byte offset of the arena cursor.
138:     pub fn arena_cursor(&self) -> u32 {
139:         self.u32(memory::OFF_ARENA_CURSOR)
140:     }
141: }
142: 
143: /// Number of ring slots per the header.
144: fn slot_count(header: &[u8]) -> usize {
145:     header::get_u32(header, OFF_SLOT_COUNT) as usize
146: }
147: 
148: /// Ring mask per the header (slot count is a power of two).
149: fn slot_mask(header: &[u8]) -> usize {
150:     let slots = slot_count(header);
151:     debug_assert!(slots.is_power_of_two());
152:     slots - 1
153: }
154: 
155: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
156: // Guest (producer)
157: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
158: 
159: /// Producer side: the guest engine writing opcodes and arena data into shared
160: /// linear memory. Owns the header, ring, and arena regions as disjoint slices.
161: pub struct Guest<'a> {
162:     header: &'a mut [u8],
163:     slots: &'a mut [u8],
164:     /// Host → guest event ring (guest reads raw inputs here).
165:     event_slots: &'a mut [u8],
166:     arena: &'a mut [u8],
167:     /// Host → guest event arena (host-owned bump; the guest resolves `TEXT_CHANGED`
168:     /// text here over the shared ring).
169:     event_arena: &'a mut [u8],
170:     /// Write cursor captured at `begin_frame`.
171:     frame_start: u32,
172: }
173: 
174: impl<'a> Guest<'a> {
175:     /// Create a guest view over the linear memory. `init_memory` MUST have been
176:     /// called on the same memory beforehand.
177:     pub fn new(mem: &'a mut [u8], layout: &MemoryLayout) -> Self {
178:         let (header, rest) = mem.split_at_mut(memory::HEADER_SIZE);
179:         let (slots, rest) = rest.split_at_mut(layout.ring_bytes());
180:         let (event_slots, rest) = rest.split_at_mut(layout.event_ring_bytes());
181:         let (arena, event_arena) = rest.split_at_mut(layout.arena_bytes);
182:         let frame_start = header::get_u32(header, OFF_WRITE_CURSOR);
183:         Self {
184:             header,
185:             slots,
186:             event_slots,
187:             arena,
188:             event_arena,
189:             frame_start,
190:         }
191:     }
192: 
193:     fn mask(&self) -> usize {
194:         slot_mask(self.header)
195:     }
196: 
197:     /// Record the start of a new frame.
198:     pub fn begin_frame(&mut self) {
199:         self.frame_start = header::get_u32(self.header, OFF_WRITE_CURSOR);
200:     }
201: 
202:     /// Number of opcodes written since the last `begin_frame`.
203:     pub fn pending(&self) -> usize {
204:         let write = header::get_u32(self.header, OFF_WRITE_CURSOR);
205:         let mask = self.mask() as u32;
206:         (write.wrapping_sub(self.frame_start) & mask) as usize
207:     }
208: 
209:     /// End the frame: increments `frameCount`.
210:     pub fn end_frame(&mut self) {
211:         let count = header::get_u32(self.header, OFF_FRAME_COUNT);
212:         header::set_u32(self.header, OFF_FRAME_COUNT, count.wrapping_add(1));
213:     }
214: 
215:     /// Total frames produced so far.
216:     pub fn frame_count(&self) -> u32 {
217:         header::get_u32(self.header, OFF_FRAME_COUNT)
218:     }
219: 
220:     // --- TREE ---
221: 
222:     pub fn create_node(&mut self, node_id: u32, component_type: u16) -> Result<(), RingError> {
223:         ring_fn::push_create_node(self.slots, self.header, self.mask(), node_id, component_type)
224:     }
225: 
226:     pub fn delete_node(&mut self, node_id: u32) -> Result<(), RingError> {
227:         ring_fn::push_delete_node(self.slots, self.header, self.mask(), node_id)
228:     }
229: 
230:     pub fn insert_child(&mut self, parent: u32, child: u32, index: u32) -> Result<(), RingError> {
231:         ring_fn::push_insert_child(self.slots, self.header, self.mask(), parent, child, index)
232:     }
233: 
234:     pub fn remove_child(&mut self, parent: u32, child: u32) -> Result<(), RingError> {
235:         ring_fn::push_remove_child(self.slots, self.header, self.mask(), parent, child)
236:     }
237: 
238:     pub fn move_child(
239:         &mut self,
240:         parent: u32,
241:         child: u32,
242:         new_index: u32,
243:     ) -> Result<(), RingError> {
244:         ring_fn::push_move_child(self.slots, self.header, self.mask(), parent, child, new_index)
245:     }
246: 
247:     // --- Raw opcode push (guest → host) ---
248: 
249:     /// Push a caller-built raw opcode into the ring. This is the escape hatch
250:     /// for foreign hosts (C ABI / FFM) that construct the 16-byte opcode
251:     /// themselves and write it into the shared ring in place.
252:     pub fn push_opcode(&mut self, op: Opcode) -> Result<(), RingError> {
253:         ring_fn::push(self.slots, self.header, self.mask(), &op)
254:     }
255: 
256:     // --- STYLE ---
257: 
258:     pub fn set_property(
259:         &mut self,
260:         node_id: u32,
261:         property_id: u16,
262:         value_type: u8,
263:         value: u32,
264:     ) -> Result<(), RingError> {
265:         ring_fn::push_set_property(
266:             self.slots,
267:             self.header,
268:             self.mask(),
269:             node_id,
270:             property_id,
271:             value_type,
272:             value,
273:         )
274:     }
275: 
276:     /// Set a node's text content via the arena.
277:     pub fn set_text(&mut self, node_id: u32, text: &str) -> Result<u32, RingError> {
278:         let arena_ref = arena_fn::alloc_str(self.arena, self.header, text).map_err(|_| RingError::Full)?;
279:         ring_fn::push_set_text(self.slots, self.header, self.mask(), node_id, arena_ref)?;
280:         Ok(arena_ref)
281:     }
282: 
283:     /// Set a node's date value via `PARAMETER::SET_DATE` (draft): `days` since the
284:     /// epoch (I32, pre-1970 negative) and `millis` of day (U32, 0..86,400,000).
285:     pub fn set_date(&mut self, node_id: u32, days: i32, millis: u32) -> Result<(), RingError> {
286:         let op = Opcode::new(
287:             category::PARAMETER,
288:             crate::parameter::SET_DATE,
289:             0,
290:             node_id,
291:             days as u32,
292:             millis,
293:         );
294:         ring_fn::push(self.slots, self.header, self.mask(), &op)
295:     }
296: 
297:     /// Override a design token globally via `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`:
298:     /// `path` (arena string) → `value` of `value_type`. Applies everywhere the
299:     /// renderer resolves tokens (spec/TOKENS.md). A `dark.`-prefixed path
300:     /// overrides the dark variant. Returns the arena offset of the path.
301:     pub fn set_design_token(
302:         &mut self,
303:         path: &str,
304:         value_type: u8,
305:         value: u32,
306:     ) -> Result<u32, RingError> {
307:         let arena_ref = arena_fn::alloc_str(self.arena, self.header, path)
308:             .map_err(|_| RingError::Full)?;
309:         let op = Opcode::new(
310:             category::PARAMETER,
311:             crate::parameter::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN,
312:             0,
313:             arena_ref,
314:             u32::from(value_type),
315:             value,
316:         );
317:         ring_fn::push(self.slots, self.header, self.mask(), &op)?;
318:         Ok(arena_ref)
319:     }
320: 
321:     /// Override a design token with a **STRING value** via `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`
322:     /// (spec/TOKENS.md): both the token path and the value are arena strings —
323:     /// `A` = path ref, `B` = `STRING` value type, `C` = value ref. Returns the
324:     /// arena offset of the path.
325:     pub fn set_design_token_string(
326:         &mut self,
327:         path: &str,
328:         value: &str,
329:     ) -> Result<u32, RingError> {
330:         let arena_ref = arena_fn::alloc_str(self.arena, self.header, path)
331:             .map_err(|_| RingError::Full)?;
332:         let value_ref = arena_fn::alloc_str(self.arena, self.header, value)
333:             .map_err(|_| RingError::Full)?;
334:         let op = Opcode::new(
335:             category::PARAMETER,
336:             crate::parameter::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN,
337:             0,
338:             arena_ref,
339:             u32::from(crate::value_type::STRING),
340:             value_ref,
341:         );
342:         ring_fn::push(self.slots, self.header, self.mask(), &op)?;
343:         Ok(arena_ref)
344:     }
345: 
346:     /// Allocate arbitrary bytes into the arena, returning the offset.
347:     pub fn alloc(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<u32, ArenaError> {
348:         arena_fn::alloc(self.arena, self.header, bytes)
349:     }
350: 
351:     /// Allocate a string into the arena, returning the offset.
352:     pub fn alloc_str(&mut self, s: &str) -> Result<u32, ArenaError> {
353:         arena_fn::alloc_str(self.arena, self.header, s)
354:     }
355: 
356:     // --- META ---
357: 
358:     pub fn reset(&mut self) -> Result<(), RingError> {
359:         ring_fn::push_reset(self.slots, self.header, self.mask())
360:     }
361: 
362:     // --- EVENT ingress (host → guest) ---
363: 
364:     /// Drain all pending raw-input events written by the host into the event
365:     /// ring, decoding each 16-byte `EVENT` opcode into a typed [`Event`].
366:     ///
367:     /// The guest (app/engine) polls this to receive renderer-reported inputs.
368:     pub fn drain_events(&mut self) -> Vec<Event> {
369:         let mask = self.mask();
370:         let ops = ring_fn::read_events(&self.event_slots, self.header, mask);
371:         ops.into_iter()
372:             .filter_map(|op| crate::events::decode_event(&op, self.event_arena))
373:             .collect()
374:     }
375: 
376:     /// Drain raw `EVENT`-category opcodes from the host → guest event ring as
377:     /// their 16-byte wire form (no decoding). Used by foreign hosts that want
378:     /// the raw bytes.
379:     pub fn drain_event_opcodes(&mut self) -> Vec<Opcode> {
380:         let mask = self.mask();
381:         ring_fn::read_events(&self.event_slots, self.header, mask)
382:     }
383: 
384:     /// The host → guest event arena bump cursor (diagnostics/tests).
385:     pub fn event_arena_cursor(&self) -> u32 {
386:         header::get_u32(self.header, memory::OFF_EVENT_ARENA_CURSOR)
387:     }
388: 
389:     /// Push a raw `EVENT`-category opcode into the host → guest event ring.
390:     ///
391:     /// This is the host-side write (the renderer reporting an input). Exposed
392:     /// here (guest can hold the ring too) so a C-ABI shim can inject raw event
393:     /// opcodes without round-tripping through the typed [`Event`] enum.
394:     pub fn push_event_opcode(&mut self, op: Opcode) -> Result<(), RingError> {
395:         ring_fn::push_event(self.event_slots, self.header, self.mask(), &op)
396:     }
397: }
398: 
399: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
400: // Host (consumer)
401: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
402: 
403: /// A completed frame produced by the guest: a sequence of opcodes plus arena
404: /// access.
405: ///
406: /// `Frame` is the **transport seam**: both the shared-memory ring (`Host`) and
407: /// network batch decoders produce frame views, so consumers such as
408: /// `RenderTree::apply_frame` work identically regardless of origin.
409: pub struct Frame<'a> {
410:     slots: &'a [u8],
411:     arena: &'a [u8],
412:     start: usize,
413:     end: usize,
414: }
415: 
416: impl<'a> Frame<'a> {
417:     /// Construct a frame view over contiguous 16-byte opcode slots plus an
418:     /// arena region (`start`/`end` are byte offsets into `slots`).
419:     ///
420:     /// Used by transport backends to produce `Frame` views over their own
421:     /// buffers; `Host` builds these internally from the ring.
422:     pub fn from_parts(slots: &'a [u8], arena: &'a [u8], start: usize, end: usize) -> Self {
423:         Self {
424:             slots,
425:             arena,
426:             start,
427:             end,
428:         }
429:     }
430: 
431:     /// Iterate the opcodes in this frame, in order.
432:     pub fn opcodes(&self) -> FrameIter<'a> {
433:         FrameIter {
434:             slots: self.slots,
435:             cursor: self.start,
436:             end: self.end,
437:         }
438:     }
439: 
440:     /// Number of opcodes in the frame.
441:     pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
442:         (self.end - self.start) / Opcode::SIZE
443:     }
444: 
445:     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
446:         self.len() == 0
447:     }
448: 
449:     /// Read an arena entry by offset (see `Guest::alloc` / `Guest::alloc_str`).
450:     pub fn arena_get(&self, offset: u32) -> Result<&'a [u8], ArenaError> {
451:         arena_fn::get(self.arena, offset)
452:     }
453: 
454:     /// Read an arena string by offset.
455:     pub fn arena_str(&self, offset: u32) -> Result<&'a str, ArenaError> {
456:         arena_fn::get_str(self.arena, offset)
457:     }
458: 
459:     /// The full arena region (for transport serialization of arena deltas).
460:     pub fn arena(&self) -> &'a [u8] {
461:         self.arena
462:     }
463: }
464: 
465: /// Iterator over the opcodes in a `Frame`.
466: pub struct FrameIter<'a> {
467:     slots: &'a [u8],
468:     cursor: usize,
469:     end: usize,
470: }
471: 
472: impl<'a> Iterator for FrameIter<'a> {
473:     type Item = Opcode;
474: 
475:     fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Opcode> {
476:         if self.cursor >= self.end {
477:             return None;
478:         }
479:         let bytes: [u8; 16] = self.slots[self.cursor..self.cursor + 16].try_into().unwrap();
480:         self.cursor += 16;
481:         Some(Opcode::from_bytes(&bytes))
482:     }
483: }
484: 
485: /// Consumer side: the host renderer reading completed frames.
486: ///
487: /// SPSC contract: the host never reads past the producer's published
488: /// `writeCursor`, and the producer never overwrites an unconsumed `readCursor`.
489: /// If the host is slow, multiple produced frames are coalesced into one `Frame`
490: /// (opcodes remain in order); the `frameCount` simply signals "new data".
491: pub struct Host<'a> {
492:     header: &'a mut [u8],
493:     slots: &'a [u8],
494:     /// Host → guest event ring (host writes raw inputs here).
495:     event_slots: &'a mut [u8],
496:     arena: &'a [u8],
497:     /// Host → guest event arena (host-owned bump; the host writes event string
498:     /// payloads here, e.g. `TEXT_CHANGED` text over the shared ring).
499:     event_arena: &'a mut [u8],
500:     /// Number of frames already consumed by this host view.
501:     consumed: u32,
502: }
503: 
504: impl<'a> Host<'a> {
505:     /// Create a host view over the linear memory.
506:     pub fn new(mem: &'a mut [u8], layout: &MemoryLayout) -> Self {
507:         let (header, rest) = mem.split_at_mut(memory::HEADER_SIZE);
508:         let (slots, rest) = rest.split_at_mut(layout.ring_bytes());
509:         let (event_slots, rest) = rest.split_at_mut(layout.event_ring_bytes());
510:         let (arena, event_arena) = rest.split_at_mut(layout.arena_bytes);
511:         let slots: &'a [u8] = slots;
512:         let arena: &'a [u8] = arena;
513:         Self {
514:             header,
515:             slots,
516:             event_slots,
517:             arena,
518:             event_arena,
519:             consumed: 0,
520:         }
521:     }
522: 
523:     /// Total frames produced by the guest (for diagnostics).
524:     pub fn frame_count(&self) -> u32 {
525:         header::get_u32(self.header, OFF_FRAME_COUNT)
526:     }
527: 
528:     /// Consume all frames produced since the last call, advancing `readCursor`.
529:     ///
530:     /// Returns at most one `Frame` (all new opcodes since the last drain). If
531:     /// the producer produced multiple frames before this call they coalesce.
532:     pub fn frames(&mut self) -> Vec<Frame<'a>> {
533:         let frame_count = header::get_u32(self.header, OFF_FRAME_COUNT);
534:         if self.consumed >= frame_count {
535:             return Vec::new();
536:         }
537:         let mask = slot_mask(self.header);
538:         let start = ring_fn::cursor(self.header, OFF_READ_CURSOR, mask);
539:         let end = ring_fn::cursor(self.header, OFF_WRITE_CURSOR, mask);
540: 
541:         // The POC producer flushes before the ring fills, so `end >= start`
542:         // always holds. Guard against a wrapped ring by draining nothing; a
543:         // wrapped producer must flush first (see OPCODE.md backpressure).
544:         if end < start {
545:             return Vec::new();
546:         }
547: 
548:         // No new opcodes since the last drain (readCursor == writeCursor). This
549:         // also covers a freshly-created host view whose `consumed` counter
550:         // starts at 0 but whose cursors have already been drained by an earlier
551:         // view — without this, `next_frame` would return empty frames forever.
552:         if start == end {
553:             return Vec::new();
554:         }
555: 
556:         let frames = vec![Frame {
557:             slots: self.slots,
558:             arena: self.arena,
559:             start: start * Opcode::SIZE,
560:             end: end * Opcode::SIZE,
561:         }];
562: 
563:         header::set_u32(self.header, OFF_READ_CURSOR, end as u32);
564:         self.consumed = frame_count;
565: 
566:         // A `META::RESET` invalidates prior state: reset the host → guest event
567:         // arena cursor so the host starts bump-allocating fresh (matching the
568:         // guest arena's reset-on-RESET semantics).
569:         let reset_seen = self.slots[start * Opcode::SIZE..end * Opcode::SIZE]
570:             .chunks_exact(Opcode::SIZE)
571:             .any(|slot| {
572:                 let bytes: [u8; 16] = slot.try_into().unwrap();
573:                 let op = Opcode::from_bytes(&bytes);
574:                 op.category() == category::META && op.command() == crate::meta::RESET
575:             });
576:         if reset_seen {
577:             memory::header::set_u32(self.header, memory::OFF_EVENT_ARENA_CURSOR, 0);
578:         }
579: 
580:         frames
581:     }
582: 
583:     /// Write a raw-input event (host → guest) into the event ring, encoded as a
584:     /// 16-byte `EVENT` opcode. The renderer reports inputs here; the guest
585:     /// drains them via [`Guest::drain_events`].
586:     ///
587:     /// `TextChanged` text and `Navigate` URLs are bump-allocated into the
588:     /// host → guest **event arena** and referenced by their absolute offset in
589:     /// `B` (the `SET_TEXT` shared-memory convention); the guest resolves them
590:     /// from the same region. If the event arena is full the event is rejected
591:     /// with [`RingError::Full`] (backpressure).
592:     pub fn send_event(&mut self, event: &Event) -> Result<(), RingError> {
593:         let mask = slot_mask(self.header);
594:         let op = match event {
595:             Event::TextChanged { target, value } => {
596:                 let offset = crate::arena::alloc_event(&mut self.event_arena, self.header, value.as_bytes())
597:                     .map_err(|_| RingError::Full)?;
598:                 Opcode::new(category::EVENT, crate::event::TEXT_CHANGED, 0, *target, offset, 0)
599:             }
600:             Event::Navigate { url: Some(url) } => {
601:                 let offset = crate::arena::alloc_event(&mut self.event_arena, self.header, url.as_bytes())
602:                     .map_err(|_| RingError::Full)?;
603:                 Opcode::new(
604:                     category::EVENT,
605:                     crate::event::NAVIGATE,
606:                     crate::flag::NAVIGATE_URL,
607:                     0,
608:                     offset,
609:                     0,
610:                 )
611:             }
612:             _ => event.encode(),
613:         };
614:         ring_fn::push_event(self.event_slots, self.header, mask, &op)
615:     }
616: }

618: #[cfg(test)]
619: mod tests {
620:     use super::*;
621:     use crate::constants::{category, component_type, property_id, value_type};
622:     use alloc::vec;
623: 
624:     #[test]
625:     fn guest_host_round_trip() {
626:         let layout = MemoryLayout::default();
627:         let mut mem = vec![0u8; layout.total_bytes()];
628:         init_memory(&mut mem, &layout);
629: 
630:         let mut guest = Guest::new(&mut mem, &layout);
631:         guest.begin_frame();
632:         guest.create_node(1, component_type::VSTACK).unwrap();
633:         guest.insert_child(0, 1, APPEND).unwrap();
634:         guest.set_property(1, property_id::SPACING, value_type::F32, 4.0f32.to_bits()).unwrap();
635:         guest
636:             .set_property(1, property_id::PADDING, value_type::F32, 8.0f32.to_bits())
637:             .unwrap();
638:         let arena_ref = guest.set_text(1, "Hello").unwrap();
639:         assert_eq!(guest.pending(), 5);
640:         guest.end_frame();
641:         assert_eq!(guest.frame_count(), 1);
642: 
643:         let mut host = Host::new(&mut mem, &layout);
644:         assert_eq!(host.frame_count(), 1);
645:         let frames = host.frames();
646:         assert_eq!(frames.len(), 1);
647:         let frame = &frames[0];
648:         let ops: Vec<Opcode> = frame.opcodes().collect();

1: //! Reactive signals (Angular-style).
2: //!
3: //! A [`Signal`] is a piece of application state owned by the engine. Retained
4: //! tree nodes bind their text or a property to a signal via [`SignalId`]; the
5: //! engine records those dependencies during emission, so when a signal's value
6: //! changes, only the nodes that read it re-emit their deltas.
7: //!
8: //! Signals live here (in `no_std` core) so any host — Rust, the native C ABI,
9: //! a future WASM/browser guest — shares the same reactive runtime.
10: 
11: use alloc::string::String;
12: use alloc::vec::Vec;
13: 
14: /// A signal's value: one of the protocol value kinds.
15: ///
16: /// Property bindings pack to a `SET_PROPERTY` value (u32); text bindings use
17: /// [`SignalValue::Str`]. The richer kinds (`Bool`, `Enum`) are ergonomic typing
18: /// at the host boundary — they still collapse onto the wire's `u32` value.
19: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
20: pub enum SignalValue {
21:     /// A float property (spacing, font_size, padding, opacity, size hints…).
22:     F32(f32),
23:     /// A raw u32 property (color `0xAARRGGBB`, an `EVENT_LISTENERS` mask, …).
24:     U32(u32),
25:     /// A boolean property (visible, clips_to_bounds, …).
26:     Bool(bool),
27:     /// An enum property wire value (alignment, text alignment, truncation, …).
28:     Enum(u8),
29:     /// A string (text content, font family).
30:     Str(String),
31: }
32: 
33: impl SignalValue {
34:     /// Pack this value as a `SET_PROPERTY` `u32` value. `None` for [`Str`],
35:     /// which is only valid for text bindings.
36:     pub fn to_property_u32(&self) -> Option<u32> {
37:         match self {
38:             SignalValue::F32(f) => Some(f.to_bits()),
39:             SignalValue::U32(u) => Some(*u),
40:             SignalValue::Bool(b) => Some(if *b { 1.0f32 } else { 0.0f32 }.to_bits()),
41:             SignalValue::Enum(e) => Some((*e as f32).to_bits()),
42:             SignalValue::Str(_) => None,
43:         }
44:     }
45: 
46:     /// The text for a text binding. `None` for non-`Str` values.
47:     pub fn to_text(&self) -> Option<&str> {
48:         match self {
49:             SignalValue::Str(s) => Some(s.as_str()),
50:             _ => None,
51:         }
52:     }
53: }

55: /// A stable, non-generic handle to a signal (an index into the engine's
56: /// [`SignalStore`]). This is the FFI-safe handle handed to foreign hosts.

58: pub struct SignalId(pub u32);

62: pub enum Dep {
63:     /// The node's text is bound to the signal.
64:     Text { node: u32 },
65:     /// A node property is bound to the signal.
66:     Property { node: u32, prop: u16 },
67: }

70: struct SignalCell {
71:     value: SignalValue,
72:     /// Reverse dependency index: the node bindings that read this signal.
73:     deps: Vec<Dep>,
74: }

76: /// Owns signal storage plus the reverse dependency index (`signal -> deps`).
77: ///
78: /// The engine rebuilds the index during each full emit; between emits, the
79: /// index lets `set` find exactly the nodes that depend on a changed signal.
80: #[derive(Debug, Default)]
81: pub struct SignalStore {
82:     cells: Vec<SignalCell>,
83: }

85: impl SignalStore {
86:     /// Create a new signal with an initial value, returning its handle.
87:     pub fn create(&mut self, value: SignalValue) -> SignalId {
88:         let id = SignalId(self.cells.len() as u32);
89:         self.cells.push(SignalCell {
90:             value,
91:             deps: Vec::new(),
92:         });
93:         id

97:     pub fn set(&mut self, id: SignalId, value: SignalValue) -> bool {

99:             if cell.value != value {

101:                 return true;
102:             }
103:         }
104:         false
105:     }

108:     pub fn get(&self, id: SignalId) -> Option<&SignalValue> {
109:         self.cells.get(id.0 as usize).map(|c| &c.value)
110:     }

113:     pub fn deps(&self, id: SignalId) -> &[Dep] {

117:             .unwrap_or(&[])

1: //! C ABI for the Pathland native host.
2: //!
3: //! Foreign host languages (Swift, Java, C#, …) link this `cdylib` and call the
4: //! `pathland_native_*` functions. The surface is the **flat world** — no
5: //! per-component wrappers — and the ring is exposed as a raw pointer + length so
6: //! the foreign driver reads opcodes **in place** (zero-copy).
7: //!
8: //! ```c
9: //! void* h = pathland_native_create();
10: //! pathland_native_create_node(h, 1, 2);            // 2 = vstack
11: //! pathland_native_create_node(h, 2, 3);            // 3 = text
12: //! pathland_native_set_text(h, 2, "Hello");
13: //! pathland_native_insert_child(h, 1, 2, UINT32_MAX);
14: //! pathland_native_emit(h);
15: //! // read opcodes from pathland_native_ring_ptr(h) (header at offset 0)
16: //! pathland_native_destroy(h);
17: //! ```
18: 
19: use std::ffi::{c_char, c_void, CStr};

21: use pathland_engine::{SignalId, SignalValue};

23: use super::{component_from_id, NativeHost};

25: /// Opaque handle to a [`NativeHost`].
26: pub type HostHandle = *mut c_void;
27: 
28: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
29: // Lifetime
30: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
31: 
32: /// Create a native host over a fresh zero-copy shared ring. Returns an opaque
33: /// handle (non-null on success).
34: #[no_mangle]
35: pub extern "C" fn pathland_native_create() -> HostHandle {
36:     let host = Box::new(NativeHost::new());
37:     Box::into_raw(host) as HostHandle
38: }
39: 
40: /// Destroy a native host previously created by [`pathland_native_create`].
41: #[no_mangle]
42: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_native_destroy(host: HostHandle) {
43:     if !host.is_null() {
44:         drop(Box::from_raw(host as *mut NativeHost));
45:     }
46: }
47: 
48: fn as_host<'a>(host: HostHandle) -> &'a mut NativeHost {
49:     unsafe { &mut *(host as *mut NativeHost) }
50: }
51: 
52: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
53: // Flat builder (variants as raw u32)
54: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
55: 
56: /// `component_id` here is the raw protocol component id (hstack=1, vstack=2,
57: /// text=3, button=4, spacer=8). Returns 1 on success, 0 on bad component.
58: #[no_mangle]
59: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_native_create_node(
60:     host: HostHandle,
61:     id: u32,
62:     component: u32,
63: ) -> u8 {
64:     let Some(component) = component_from_id(component) else {
65:         return 0;
66:     };
67:     as_host(host).create_node(id, component);
68:     1
69: }
70: 
71: #[no_mangle]
72: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_native_insert_child(
73:     host: HostHandle,
74:     parent: u32,
75:     child: u32,
76:     index: u32,
77: ) -> u8 {
78:     as_host(host).insert_child(parent, child, index);
79:     1
80: }

85:     1
86: }

88: /// Set a node's text content from a NUL-terminated UTF-8 C string.
89: #[no_mangle]
90: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_native_set_text(
91:     host: HostHandle,
92:     id: u32,
93:     text: *const c_char,
94: ) -> u8 {
95:     if text.is_null() {
96:         return 0;
97:     }
98:     let text = CStr::from_ptr(text).to_string_lossy().into_owned();
99:     as_host(host).set_text(id, &text);
100:     1
101: }

103: /// Set a property with a raw u32 value (bit pattern — floats are passed via
104: /// `pathland_native_set_property_f32`).

108:     id: u32,

133: /// was written.
134: #[no_mangle]
135: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_native_emit(host: HostHandle) -> u8 {
136:     if as_host(host).emit() {
137:         1
138:     } else {
139:         0
140:     }
141: }

143: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
144: // Zero-copy ring access
145: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
146: 
147: /// Return a pointer to the shared linear memory (header | ring | arena) so a
148: /// foreign driver can read opcodes in place. Never null; the header layout is
149: /// the stable wire layout in `spec/OPCODE.md` (frameCount/readCursor/
150: /// writeCursor/ringOffset/arenaOffset at their documented offsets).
151: #[no_mangle]
152: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_native_ring_ptr(host: HostHandle) -> *const u8 {
153:     let host = as_host(host);
154:     host.ring_buffer().as_ptr()
155: }
156: 
157: /// Total length in bytes of the shared linear memory buffer.
158: #[no_mangle]
159: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_native_ring_len(host: HostHandle) -> usize {
160:     let host = as_host(host);
161:     host.ring_buffer().len()
162: }
163: 
164: /// Convenience: return the total buffer length of the default layout.
165: #[no_mangle]
166: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_native_layout_bytes(host: HostHandle) -> usize {
167:     let host = as_host(host);
168:     host.layout().total_bytes()
169: }
170: 
171: /// Read the root node id (u32_MAX = none).
172: #[no_mangle]
173: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_native_root_id(host: HostHandle) -> u32 {
174:     as_host(host).root_id().unwrap_or(u32::MAX)
175: }
176: 
177: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
178: // Raw-input events (host → guest)
179: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
180: 
181: /// Drain pending raw-input events written by a renderer into the host → guest
182: /// event ring, writing each as its raw 16-byte `EVENT` opcode
183: /// (`[category][command][flags:u16][A:u32][B:u32][C:u32]`, little-endian) into
184: /// `out`. Returns the number of events written (≤ `max`).
185: ///
186: /// `out` must point to at least `max * 16` writable bytes. This is the generic
187: /// event path: the renderer only writes `EVENT` opcodes; the host drains them
188: /// here, symmetric with how a driver reads frame opcodes via
189: /// [`pathland_native_ring_ptr`].
190: #[no_mangle]
191: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_native_drain_events(
192:     host: HostHandle,
193:     out: *mut u8,
194:     max: u32,
195: ) -> u32 {
196:     if out.is_null() || max == 0 {
197:         return 0;
198:     }
199:     let events = as_host(host).drain_events();
200:     let n = events.len().min(max as usize);
201:     for (i, ev) in events.into_iter().take(n).enumerate() {
202:         let bytes = ev.encode().to_bytes();
203:         // SAFETY: `out` points to ≥ max*16 writable bytes; we write ≤ max slots.
204:         std::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(bytes.as_ptr(), out.add(i * 16), 16);
205:     }
206:     n as u32
207: }

211: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

215: }

218: #[no_mangle]

1: //! Shared-memory ring transport (zero-copy, SPSC).
2: //!
3: //! The producer (opcode engine) and consumer (native driver) share one linear
4: //! memory buffer containing the ring + arena. The producer writes 16-byte
5: //! opcodes via `pathland_core::Guest`; the consumer reads completed frames via
6: //! `pathland_core::Host`. No copying, no batching, no serialization — this is
7: //! the high-performance local path.
8: 
9: use pathland_core::{init_memory, Guest, Host, MemoryLayout};
10: 
11: use crate::traits::{DriverTransport, FrameSource, OpcodeBatch, TransportError};
12: 
13: /// A zero-copy SPSC shared-memory ring transport.
14: ///
15: /// Owns the linear-memory buffer (header + ring + arena). Producers and
16: /// consumers are granted short-lived `Guest`/`Host` views over the same buffer
17: /// via the borrowed methods, so opcodes flow in place with no copies.
18: #[derive(Debug)]
19: pub struct RingTransport {
20:     /// Shared linear memory (header | ring | arena).
21:     mem: Vec<u8>,
22:     /// Ring/arena geometry.
23:     layout: MemoryLayout,
24: }
25: 
26: impl RingTransport {
27:     /// Create a ring transport with a default layout and a zeroed header.
28:     pub fn new() -> Self {
29:         let layout = MemoryLayout::default();
30:         let mut mem = vec![0u8; layout.total_bytes()];
31:         init_memory(&mut mem, &layout);
32:         Self { mem, layout }
33:     }
34: 
35:     /// Create a ring transport over a caller-provided buffer/layout.
36:     pub fn with_buffer(mem: Vec<u8>, layout: MemoryLayout) -> Self {
37:         Self { mem, layout }
38:     }

40:     /// The memory layout (region geometry).
41:     pub fn layout(&self) -> &MemoryLayout {
42:         &self.layout
43:     }
44: 
45:     /// Create a producer view over the shared buffer (writes opcodes + arena).
46:     ///
47:     /// Drop the returned `Guest` before calling `next_frame`; producer and
48:     /// consumer must not overlap borrows.
49:     pub fn producer(&mut self) -> Guest<'_> {
50:         Guest::new(&mut self.mem, &self.layout)
51:     }
52: 
53:     /// Peak at the raw underlying buffer (for embedding/custom transports).
54:     pub fn buffer(&self) -> &[u8] {
55:         &self.mem
56:     }
57: }

70:             Some(frame) => Ok(Some(OpcodeBatch::new(

234:         let arena = frame.arena_str(arena_ref).expect("arena string");

245:             "arena string must be borrowed from the shared ring (ptr {str_ptr:#x} outside {buf_base:#x}..{buf_end:#x})"

248:         // No per-opcode copying: a handful of O(1) bookkeeping allocations is
249:         // fine; anything O(opcodes) would mean the opcode stream was copied.
250:         assert!(
251:             allocs < OPCODES,
252:             "reading {OPCODES} opcodes must not copy them (allocations: {allocs})"
253:         );

1: //! # pathland-core-transport
2: //!
3: //! How Pathland opcodes are transported from the guest engine to host
4: //! renderers. There are two peer backends:
5: //!
6: //! - **Shared memory** (desktop/native/WASM): the ring buffer + arena in
7: //!   `pathland-core` (`Guest`/`Host`). Zero-copy. This crate treats it as
8: //!   the local transport — no duplication.
9: //! - **Network batch** (SSR → browser): opcodes + string data serialized into
10: //!   **batches**.
11: //!
12: //! There are two network codecs, for two different relationships between the
13: //! producer and the consumer:
14: //!
15: //! - **Self-contained frames** ([`encode_frame`] / [`decode_frame`]) — each
16: //!   batch carries its own string section and `SET_TEXT` references strings by
17: //!   a *relative* offset into that section. The consumer needs **no prior
18: //!   state**: every message is independent. This is the streaming codec used
19: //!   for live deltas over WebSocket.
20: //! - **Arena-delta batches** ([`encode_batch`] / [`BatchEncoder`] /
21: //!   [`BatchDecoder`]) — the batch carries only the bytes *appended* to the
22: //!   arena since the previous batch, and `SET_TEXT` references absolute arena
23: //!   offsets. The consumer mirrors the arena so those offsets stay valid. This
24: //!   mirrors the shared-memory arena over a wire and is the ring-compatible
25: //!   codec (kept for a future WASM/embedded guest).
26: //!
27: //! ## Batch wire format (both codecs share the header)
28: //!
29: //! ```text
30: //! magic "PLPL" (u32 LE) | version (u16) | flags (u16) | frameCount (u32)
31: //! | opcodeCount (u32) | opcodes (16 B × opcodeCount) | stringsLen (u32)
32: //! | string bytes (length-prefixed entries: [u32 len][bytes])
33: //! ```
34: //!
35: //! For a self-contained frame the trailing section is that frame's own string
36: //! table; for an arena-delta batch it is the arena bytes appended since the
37: //! last batch.
38: //!
39: //! ## Example (producer)
40: //!
41: //! ```no_run
42: //! use pathland_core_transport::{Batcher, BatchPolicy, BatchEncoder};
43: //! use std::time::Duration;
44: //!
45: //! let policy = BatchPolicy::new(Duration::from_millis(4), 1400);
46: //! let mut batcher = Batcher::new(policy);
47: //! let mut encoder = BatchEncoder::new();
48: //!
49: //! // batcher.push_frame(&frame) accumulates opcodes + arena delta;
50: //! // batcher.flush() -> Option<Vec<u8>> produces the serialized batch.
51: //! ```
52: 
53: #![forbid(unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn)]
54:

56: 
57: mod batch;
58: mod batching;
59: mod conformance;
60: mod net;
61: mod ring;
62: mod traits;
63:

65:     decode_events, decode_frame, encode_batch, encode_events, encode_frame, encode_resync, frame_from_slices,
66:     Batch, BatchDecoder, BatchEncoder,
67: };
68: pub use batching::{Batcher, BatchPolicy};
69: pub use net::NetBatchEncoder;
70: pub use ring::RingTransport;
71: pub use traits::{
72:     DriverTransport, FrameSource, InputSink, OpcodeBatch, ProtocolError, TransportError,
73: };

1: //! Transport abstraction: how opcode batches move from producer to consumer.
2: //!
3: //! The UI runtime produces renderer-neutral opcodes and knows nothing about the
4: //! transport. This module defines the boundary between:
5: //!
6: //! - the **producer** (opcode engine) that emits opcodes, and
7: //! - the **consumer** (driver) that reads them.
8: //!
9: //! Local transports (shared-memory ring) may be zero-copy; remote transports
10: //! (WebSocket/IPC) copy and serialize. Both conform to the same traits.
11: //!
12: //! The two ends are deliberately separate because a transport is often split
13: //! across a process/IPC boundary, with different backpressure and blocking
14: //! semantics on each side.
15: 
16: use pathland_core::Frame;
17: 
18: /// A single in-memory transport unit: one frame of opcodes + arena plus
19: /// transport metadata. Distinct from the raw opcode stream and from the
20: /// wire-format batch.
21: pub struct OpcodeBatch<'a> {
22:     frame: Frame<'a>,
23:     /// Transport direction bitmask (see [`crate::direction`]).
24:     direction: u16,
25: }
26: 
27: impl<'a> OpcodeBatch<'a> {
28:     /// Wrap a frame as a transport batch (guest → host by default).
29:     pub fn new(frame: Frame<'a>, direction: u16) -> Self {
30:         Self { frame, direction }
31:     }
32: 
33:     /// The frame carried by this batch.
34:     pub fn frame(&self) -> &Frame<'a> {
35:         &self.frame
36:     }
37: 
38:     /// Transport direction bitmask.
39:     pub fn direction(&self) -> u16 {
40:         self.direction
41:     }
42: }

44: /// Errors produced by a transport while sending or receiving.
45: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
46: pub enum TransportError {
47:     /// The consumer has not drained; the producer should retain and retry.
48:     Backpressure,
49:     /// The transport is closed/terminated.
50:     Closed,
51:     /// The peer violated the protocol.
52:     Protocol(ProtocolError),
53: }
54: 
55: /// Sub-errors for protocol violations.
56: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
57: pub enum ProtocolError {
58:     /// The remote sent a version this side does not support.
59:     BadVersion,
60:     /// The payload is malformed (bad magic, truncated, bad length).
61:     Malformed,
62:     /// A raw input could not be interpreted.
63:     BadInput,
64: }

66: /// Handles raw-input events arriving from the host (renderer → engine).
67: ///
68: /// The driver resolves a raw input to a node id (via hit-testing) and dispatches
69: /// it here; the transport's guest side forwards it to the guest engine.
70: pub trait InputSink {
71:     /// Deliver a raw input (host → guest).
72:     fn dispatch(&mut self, event: &pathland_core::Event);
73: }

75: /// The consumer side of a transport: the driver reads frames here.
76: ///
77: /// A transport may be blocking or non-blocking; `next_frame` reflects that.
78: /// The returned `Frame` borrows the transport's backing memory (zero-copy when

80: pub trait FrameSource {

82:     ///

84:     /// per implementation).
85:     fn next_frame(&mut self) -> Result<Option<OpcodeBatch<'_>>, TransportError>;
86: }

1: //! Batching policy and buffering for network transport.
2: //!
3: //! `Batcher` accumulates frames against a [`BatchPolicy`] and flushes a single
4: //! serialized batch when either the time interval since the first buffered
5: //! opcode elapses **or** the accumulated byte size reaches the threshold —
6: //! first trigger wins.
7: 
8: use alloc::vec::Vec;
9: use std::time::{Duration, Instant};
10: 
11: use pathland_core::Opcode;
12: 
13: use crate::batch::encode_batch;
14: use crate::direction::GUEST_TO_HOST;
15: 
16: /// Default time interval before a batch is flushed (4 ms).
17: pub const DEFAULT_MAX_INTERVAL: Duration = Duration::from_millis(4);
18: /// Default max batch byte size (conservative network frame / MTU).
19: pub const DEFAULT_MAX_BATCH_BYTES: usize = 1400;
20: 
21: /// Flush thresholds for network batching.
22: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
23: pub struct BatchPolicy {
24:     /// Flush when this much time has elapsed since the first buffered opcode.
25:     pub max_interval: Duration,
26:     /// Flush when the accumulated batch reaches this many bytes.
27:     pub max_batch_bytes: usize,
28: }
29: 
30: impl BatchPolicy {
31:     /// Create a policy from a time interval and a max batch size.
32:     pub const fn new(max_interval: Duration, max_batch_bytes: usize) -> Self {
33:         Self {
34:             max_interval,
35:             max_batch_bytes,
36:         }
37:     }
38: 
39:     /// The default policy: 4 ms interval, 1400-byte batches.
40:     pub const fn default_policy() -> Self {
41:         Self::new(DEFAULT_MAX_INTERVAL, DEFAULT_MAX_BATCH_BYTES)
42:     }
43: }
44: 
45: impl Default for BatchPolicy {
46:     fn default() -> Self {
47:         Self::default_policy()
48:     }
49: }
50: 
51: /// Accumulates frames into a batch and flushes per [`BatchPolicy`].
52: ///
53: /// The arena is append-only; the batcher ships the bytes appended since the
54: /// last flush (tracked by arena length). If the arena shrank (a `META::RESET`),
55: /// the pending arena is reset so the next flush starts fresh.
56: #[derive(Debug)]
57: pub struct Batcher {
58:     policy: BatchPolicy,
59:     /// Frame count of the first buffered frame.
60:     frame_count: u32,
61:     /// Opcodes buffered since the last flush.
62:     opcodes: Vec<Opcode>,
63:     /// Arena bytes appended since the last flush.
64:     pending_arena: Vec<u8>,
65:     /// Arena length at the last flush.
66:     last_arena_len: usize,
67:     /// When the first opcode of the current batch was buffered.
68:     started: Option<Instant>,
69:     /// Size trigger latched on push.
70:     size_triggered: bool,
71: }
72: 
73: impl Batcher {
74:     /// Create a batcher with the given policy.
75:     pub fn new(policy: BatchPolicy) -> Self {
76:         Self {
77:             policy,
78:             frame_count: 0,
79:             opcodes: Vec::new(),
80:             pending_arena: Vec::new(),
81:             last_arena_len: 0,
82:             started: None,
83:             size_triggered: false,
84:         }
85:     }
86: 
87:     /// Create a batcher with the default policy (4 ms / 1400 B).
88:     pub fn default_policy() -> Self {
89:         Self::new(BatchPolicy::default())
90:     }
91: 
92:     /// Whether no opcodes are currently buffered.
93:     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
94:         self.opcodes.is_empty()
95:     }
96: 
97:     /// Number of opcodes buffered since the last flush (diagnostics).
98:     pub fn pending_opcodes(&self) -> usize {
99:         self.opcodes.len()
100:     }
101: 
102:     /// Approximate bytes that would be shipped on flush (diagnostics).
103:     pub fn pending_bytes(&self) -> usize {
104:         self.opcodes.len() * Opcode::SIZE + self.pending_arena.len() + crate::batch::BATCH_HEADER + 4
105:     }
106: 
107:     /// Record a frame (opcodes + the arena's used portion `[0..cursor)`),
108:     /// accumulating the arena delta. Returns `true` if the size trigger fired.
109:     pub fn push_frame(&mut self, frame_count: u32, opcodes: &[Opcode], arena_used: &[u8]) -> bool {
110:         if self.started.is_none() {
111:             self.started = Some(Instant::now());
112:             self.frame_count = frame_count;
113:         }
114:         if arena_used.len() < self.last_arena_len {
115:             // Arena was reset; restart the pending buffer.
116:             self.pending_arena.clear();
117:             self.last_arena_len = 0;
118:         }
119:         self.pending_arena.extend_from_slice(&arena_used[self.last_arena_len..]);
120:         self.last_arena_len = arena_used.len();
121:         self.opcodes.extend_from_slice(opcodes);
122: 
123:         self.size_triggered |= self.pending_bytes() >= self.policy.max_batch_bytes;
124:         self.size_triggered
125:     }
126: 
127:     /// Whether the time interval has elapsed since the first buffered opcode.
128:     pub fn interval_elapsed(&self) -> bool {
129:         match self.started {
130:             Some(t) => t.elapsed() >= self.policy.max_interval,
131:             None => false,
132:         }
133:     }
134: 
135:     /// Serialize and reset the current buffer, returning the batch bytes.
136:     ///
137:     /// Flushes when `force` is true or either policy trigger fired. Returns
138:     /// `None` when nothing is buffered.
139:     pub fn flush(&mut self, force: bool) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
140:         if self.opcodes.is_empty() {
141:             return None;
142:         }
143:         let should_flush = force || self.size_triggered || self.interval_elapsed();
144:         if !should_flush {
145:             return None;
146:         }
147:         let bytes = encode_batch(
148:             self.frame_count,
149:             GUEST_TO_HOST,
150:             &self.opcodes,
151:             &self.pending_arena,
152:         );
153:         self.opcodes.clear();
154:         self.pending_arena.clear();
155:         self.last_arena_len = 0;
156:         self.started = None;
157:         self.size_triggered = false;
158:         Some(bytes)
159:     }
160: }

1: //! Batch wire format: encode/decode opcodes + arena delta into network batches.
2: 
3: use alloc::vec::Vec;
4: use pathland_core::{Event, Frame, Opcode, category, event, meta};
5: 
6: use crate::{BATCH_MAGIC, BATCH_VERSION};
7: 
8: /// Fixed header byte length: magic(4) + version(2) + flags(2) + frameCount(4) + opcodeCount(4).
9: pub const BATCH_HEADER: usize = 16;
10: 
11: /// Errors produced while decoding a network batch.
12: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
13: pub enum BatchError {
14:     /// The batch is shorter than the fixed header.
15:     Truncated,
16:     /// The batch magic does not match `BATCH_MAGIC`.
17:     BadMagic,
18:     /// The batch version is not supported.
19:     BadVersion,
20:     /// The opcode payload is truncated (opcodeCount × 16 exceeds the buffer).
21:     BadOpcodeCount,
22:     /// The arena delta length exceeds the remaining buffer.
23:     BadArenaLen,
24: }

26: /// A decoded network batch: opcodes plus a mirrored arena, exposed as a
27: /// `pathland_core::Frame` so consumers (`RenderTree::apply_frame`) work
28: /// exactly as with shared-memory frames.
29: pub struct Batch<'a> {
30:     frame: Frame<'a>,
31:     frame_count: u32,
32:     flags: u16,
33: }
34: 
35: impl<'a> core::fmt::Debug for Batch<'a> {
36:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
37:         f.debug_struct("Batch")
38:             .field("frame_count", &self.frame_count)
39:             .field("flags", &self.flags)
40:             .field("len", &self.len())
41:             .finish()
42:     }
43: }

45: impl<'a> Batch<'a> {
46:     /// The opcodes carried by this batch, in order.
47:     pub fn opcodes(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = Opcode> + '_ {
48:         self.frame.opcodes()
49:     }
50: 
51:     /// Number of opcodes in the batch.
52:     pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
53:         self.frame.len()
54:     }
55: 
56:     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
57:         self.frame.is_empty()
58:     }
59: 
60:     /// The guest frame count the batch spans.
61:     pub fn frame_count(&self) -> u32 {
62:         self.frame_count
63:     }
64: 
65:     /// Direction flags (see [`crate::direction`]).
66:     pub fn flags(&self) -> u16 {
67:         self.flags
68:     }
69: 
70:     /// View this batch as a `Frame` (the transport seam).
71:     pub fn as_frame(&self) -> &Frame<'a> {
72:         &self.frame
73:     }
74: 
75:     /// Read an arena entry by offset (see `Frame::arena_get`).
76:     pub fn arena_get(&self, offset: u32) -> Result<&'a [u8], pathland_core::ArenaError> {
77:         self.frame.arena_get(offset)
78:     }
79: 
80:     /// Read an arena string by offset.
81:     pub fn arena_str(&self, offset: u32) -> Result<&'a str, pathland_core::ArenaError> {
82:         self.frame.arena_str(offset)
83:     }
84: }

86: /// Serialize one batch from opcodes + an arena delta (bytes appended since the
87: /// previous batch). Stateless; see [`BatchEncoder`] for cursor tracking.
88: pub fn encode_batch(
89:     frame_count: u32,
90:     flags: u16,
91:     opcodes: &[Opcode],
92:     arena_delta: &[u8],
93: ) -> Vec<u8> {
94:     let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(BATCH_HEADER + opcodes.len() * Opcode::SIZE + arena_delta.len() + 4);
95:     out.extend_from_slice(&BATCH_MAGIC.to_le_bytes());
96:     out.extend_from_slice(&BATCH_VERSION.to_le_bytes());
97:     out.extend_from_slice(&flags.to_le_bytes());
98:     out.extend_from_slice(&frame_count.to_le_bytes());
99:     out.extend_from_slice(&(opcodes.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
100:     for op in opcodes {
101:         out.extend_from_slice(&op.to_bytes());
102:     }
103:     out.extend_from_slice(&(arena_delta.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
104:     out.extend_from_slice(arena_delta);
105:     out
106: }

108: /// Fields parsed from a batch header + payload regions.
109: struct ParsedBatch<'a> {
110:     flags: u16,
111:     frame_count: u32,
112:     opcodes: &'a [u8],
113:     arena_delta: &'a [u8],
114: }
115: 
116: /// Parse a batch header, returning flags, frame count, opcode bytes and arena delta.
117: fn parse(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<ParsedBatch<'_>, BatchError> {
118:     if bytes.len() < BATCH_HEADER {
119:         return Err(BatchError::Truncated);
120:     }
121:     let magic = u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[0..4].try_into().unwrap());
122:     if magic != BATCH_MAGIC {
123:         return Err(BatchError::BadMagic);
124:     }
125:     let version = u16::from_le_bytes(bytes[4..6].try_into().unwrap());
126:     if version != BATCH_VERSION {
127:         return Err(BatchError::BadVersion);
128:     }
129:     let flags = u16::from_le_bytes(bytes[6..8].try_into().unwrap());
130:     let frame_count = u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[8..12].try_into().unwrap());
131:     let opcode_count = u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[12..16].try_into().unwrap()) as usize;
132: 
133:     let opcodes_bytes = opcode_count
134:         .checked_mul(Opcode::SIZE)
135:         .ok_or(BatchError::BadOpcodeCount)?;
136:     let opcodes_start = BATCH_HEADER;
137:     let opcodes_end = opcodes_start
138:         .checked_add(opcodes_bytes)
139:         .ok_or(BatchError::BadOpcodeCount)?;
140:     if opcodes_end > bytes.len() {
141:         return Err(BatchError::BadOpcodeCount);
142:     }
143:     let arena_len_pos = opcodes_end;
144:     if arena_len_pos + 4 > bytes.len() {
145:         return Err(BatchError::BadArenaLen);
146:     }
147:     let arena_len = u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[arena_len_pos..arena_len_pos + 4].try_into().unwrap())
148:         as usize;
149:     let arena_start = arena_len_pos + 4;
150:     let arena_end = arena_start
151:         .checked_add(arena_len)
152:         .ok_or(BatchError::BadArenaLen)?;
153:     if arena_end > bytes.len() {
154:         return Err(BatchError::BadArenaLen);
155:     }
156: 
157:     Ok(ParsedBatch {
158:         flags,
159:         frame_count,
160:         opcodes: &bytes[opcodes_start..opcodes_end],
161:         arena_delta: &bytes[arena_start..arena_end],
162:     })
163: }

165: /// A streamed network-batch encoder.
166: ///
167: /// Tracks the last arena length so successive batches carry only the bytes
168: /// appended to the bump arena since the previous batch. If the arena is reset
169: /// (shrank — see `META::RESET`), the full used arena is sent and tracking
170: /// restarts.
171: #[derive(Debug, Default)]
172: pub struct BatchEncoder {
173:     last_arena_len: usize,
174: }
175: 
176: impl BatchEncoder {
177:     /// Create a fresh encoder (no arena bytes sent yet).
178:     pub fn new() -> Self {
179:         Self { last_arena_len: 0 }
180:     }
181: 
182:     /// Encode a frame's opcodes plus the arena bytes appended since the last
183:     /// call. `arena_used` is the arena region's used portion (`[0..cursor)`).
184:     ///
185:     /// If the frame contains `META::RESET`, arena tracking restarts (the arena
186:     /// cursor returns to 0) and the full used arena is sent.
187:     pub fn encode(&mut self, frame_count: u32, opcodes: &[Opcode], arena_used: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
188:         let reset = opcodes.iter().any(|op| {
189:             op.category() == pathland_core::category::META
190:                 && op.command() == pathland_core::meta::RESET
191:         });
192:         if reset {
193:             self.last_arena_len = 0;
194:         }
195:         let delta = if arena_used.len() >= self.last_arena_len {
196:             &arena_used[self.last_arena_len..]
197:         } else {
198:             // Arena shrank unexpectedly: send the full used arena again.
199:             arena_used
200:         };
201:         let bytes = encode_batch(frame_count, crate::direction::GUEST_TO_HOST, opcodes, delta);
202:         self.last_arena_len = arena_used.len();
203:         bytes
204:     }
205: 
206:     /// The arena length already shipped (diagnostics).
207:     pub fn arena_sent(&self) -> usize {
208:         self.last_arena_len
209:     }
210: }

212: /// A streamed network-batch decoder.
213: ///
214: /// Maintains a **mirrored arena**: each batch's arena delta is appended, so
215: /// absolute `arenaRef` offsets resolve exactly as in shared memory. When a
216: /// batch contains `META::RESET`, the mirror is cleared before appending.
217: #[derive(Debug, Default)]
218: pub struct BatchDecoder {
219:     arena: Vec<u8>,
220: }
221: 
222: impl BatchDecoder {
223:     /// Create an empty decoder.
224:     pub fn new() -> Self {
225:         Self { arena: Vec::new() }
226:     }
227: 
228:     /// Decode a batch, appending its arena delta to the mirror.
229:     ///
230:     /// The returned `Batch` borrows `bytes` (opcodes) and this decoder (arena);
231:     /// keep both alive while consuming it.
232:     pub fn decode<'a>(&'a mut self, bytes: &'a [u8]) -> Result<Batch<'a>, BatchError> {
233:         let parsed = parse(bytes)?;
234: 
235:         // A META::RESET in the batch clears the renderer; reset the arena mirror
236:         // to match (offsets restart at 0 after a reset).
237:         let opcode_count = parsed.opcodes.len() / Opcode::SIZE;
238:         let reset = (0..opcode_count).any(|i| {
239:             let op = Opcode::from_bytes(parsed.opcodes[i * Opcode::SIZE..(i + 1) * Opcode::SIZE].try_into().unwrap());
240:             op.category() == pathland_core::category::META
241:                 && op.command() == pathland_core::meta::RESET
242:         });
243:         if reset {
244:             self.arena.clear();
245:         }
246:         self.arena.extend_from_slice(parsed.arena_delta);
247: 
248:         let frame = Frame::from_parts(parsed.opcodes, &self.arena, 0, parsed.opcodes.len());
249:         Ok(Batch {
250:             frame,
251:             frame_count: parsed.frame_count,
252:             flags: parsed.flags,
253:         })
254:     }
255: 
256:     /// The mirrored arena length (diagnostics).
257:     pub fn arena_len(&self) -> usize {
258:         self.arena.len()
259:     }
260: }
